answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works best when identity cost compounds over time. Each registration spends a mined proof-of-work ticket, priced like copper: cheap to try, but paid per head. A newcomer starts in a shared meadow of low-value tasks, and its voting weight grows only as independent attestations confirm its work. Misbehaviour burns the stake and marks that reputation as a cold ember, so a farm of fresh identities must repay the same cost for every fake account it wants to field.
